skill.name: when-auditing-security-use-security-analyzer
skill.description: Run multi-phase security audits that combine static analysis, dynamic checks, dependency review, secrets detection, and OWASP reporting.
skill.summary: Coordinate security scans and reports for JavaScript and TypeScript projects.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: The static matches are overwhelmingly scanner signatures, documentation examples, local temporary-file usage, or local audit commands rather than malicious behavior. I did not find evidence of credential exfiltration, destructive actions, prompt injection, or unauthorized remote targeting, but the skill does execute external tooling and can generate sensitive local reports. Static review was capped at 400/481 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 81 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Unpinned alpha dependency executed with npx
remediation.suggestion: Pin claude-flow to an audited version, document the dependency, and require user confirmation before running hooks that may execute downloaded code.

remediation.issue: Security reports can include secrets and vulnerable code snippets
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to store reports securely, redact secret values by default, and avoid copying reports to public services.

remediation.issue: Pattern-based checks can produce false positives
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear manual verification step before failing releases or reporting findings as confirmed vulnerabilities.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned External Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The workflow repeatedly invokes npx claude-flow@alpha. Running an alpha package through npx can execute code fetched from the package registry unless the user has pinned, audited, and approved that dependency.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines show direct npx execution of claude-flow@alpha in both documentation and the command script. This is a supply-chain and execution-safety concern, but it is transparent and related to the skill workflow rather than hidden malware.

semantic_findings.title: Security Reports May Contain Sensitive Findings
semantic_findings.description: The analyzer writes matched secrets, dependency data, and source snippets into local temporary files and the output report. This is expected for a scanner, but reports must be treated as sensitive artifacts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script explicitly scans for credentials and includes findings in the generated report. There is no external upload shown, so the issue is local handling and disclosure risk.

content.user_title: Run Security Audits with AI Agents
content.value_statement: Security reviews often miss issues spread across code, dependencies, runtime behavior, and secrets. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a structured audit workflow with reporting gates.
actual_capabilities: Scans JavaScript and TypeScript code for SQL injection, XSS, path traversal, and weak cryptography patterns.
Runs dependency checks with npm audit when a package.json file is present.
Searches local project files for common API keys, passwords, and credential patterns.
Checks a local application endpoint for optional dynamic testing readiness.
Generates a markdown security report with severity counts and remediation guidance.
Can compare current results with a baseline report to highlight regressions.
limitations: Dynamic testing is limited to local application checks and placeholder routines unless extended by the user.
Pattern-based scanning can produce false positives and requires human review.
The shell workflow assumes common Unix tools such as grep, jq, npm, curl, and bc are available.
It does not replace a full professional penetration test or threat model.

use_cases.title: Pre-merge security review
use_cases.description: Run a local scan before opening a pull request to catch common injection, secrets, and dependency issues.

use_cases.title: Release readiness audit
use_cases.description: Combine static checks, npm audit results, and OWASP scoring into one report before a release.

use_cases.title: Security learning workflow
use_cases.description: Use documented vulnerable and safe examples to teach teams how common web security issues appear in code.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic static scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner scan for local code issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the security analyzer to run a static scan on this project and summarize the most important findings.

prompt_templates.title: Check secrets and dependencies
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused audit before sharing a repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Run secrets detection and dependency auditing, then tell me which findings need immediate action.

prompt_templates.title: Compare against a baseline
prompt_templates.scenario: Regression review for a security report
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the security analyzer against this codebase and compare the results with my existing baseline report.

prompt_templates.title: Perform a full release audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the full security analyzer workflow with strict mode, include OWASP coverage, and produce a prioritized remediation plan.

output_examples.input: Run a static security scan before my pull request.
output: Summary of issue counts by severity.
List of likely SQL injection, XSS, path traversal, and crypto findings.

output_examples.input: Check whether this release has new security regressions.
output: Baseline comparison showing whether issue counts increased or decreased.
Dependency vulnerability summary from npm audit.
Potential credential matches found in local files.
Guidance to rotate secrets and update packages when needed.

best_practices: Run scans only on repositories and local services you are authorized to test.
Review each finding manually before treating it as a confirmed vulnerability.
Store generated reports securely because they can include sensitive file paths or code snippets.
anti_patterns: Do not run dynamic or rate-limit tests against third-party systems without written permission.
Do not paste generated reports into public tools when they contain secrets or internal paths.
Do not treat grep-based results as complete coverage for complex security issues.

faq.question: Does this skill exploit vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for authorized defensive review and local validation, not offensive exploitation.

faq.question: Can it run with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Will it scan dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. It runs npm audit when package.json exists in the selected scan path.

faq.question: Can it find all secrets?
faq.answer: No. It checks common patterns and can miss unusual formats or encrypted credentials.

faq.question: Does it send findings to external services?
faq.answer: The reviewed script writes local reports and optionally calls Claude Flow hooks. Users should review hook behavior before enabling it.

faq.question: Is manual review still required?
faq.answer: Yes. The scanner is pattern based, so humans must confirm severity, exploitability, and remediation priority.
